_help: Edexcel A level Politics (9PL0) map + the keyword rules used to tag stories. Keyword syntax: 'word' = whole word, any case; 'word*' = word + any ending; 'cs:Word' = case-sensitive; 're:regex' = regular expression (any case); 'rcs:regex' = case-sensitive regex. Weights: 3 = strong signal, 2 = medium, 1 = weak. A story gets a tag when its score reaches 'min' (default 3). 'neg' keywords subtract 2 each. context: uk | us | any | both.
specNote: Based on the Pearson Edexcel A level Politics specification (9PL0). Topic numbers follow Issue 3 (A level exams up to 2027); Issue 4 (first A level exams 2028) keeps the same topics with small changes, e.g. the closed list system replaces the supplementary vote in 3.1.

components.name: UK Politics
components.blurb: Democracy & participation, parties, electoral systems, voting behaviour & the media.

components.name: UK Government
components.blurb: The constitution, Parliament, the PM & executive, relations between the branches.

components.name: Political Ideas
components.blurb: Core ideas (Paper 1) and the non-core idea you study (Paper 2).

components.name: USA
components.blurb: Constitution & federalism, Congress, presidency, Supreme Court & rights, democracy & participation.

components.name: Global Politics
components.blurb: State & globalisation, global governance, power, regionalism & the EU, realism vs liberalism.

topics.name: The US Supreme Court and civil rights
Global governance: human rights and environmental

tags.name: Representative & direct democracy
tags.about: How well the UK's democracy works: participation, turnout, trust, petitions, referendums and citizens' assemblies.
tags.look: Turnout figures, trust polls, e-petitions debated in Parliament, recall petitions, citizens' assemblies.

tags.name: Franchise & suffrage
tags.about: Who gets to vote and how: votes at 16, voter ID, registration and debates over extending the franchise.
tags.look: Votes at 16, automatic voter registration, voter ID rules, overseas voters, prisoner voting.

tags.name: Pressure groups & other influences
tags.about: Pressure groups, think tanks, lobbyists, trade unions, protest movements and their influence on government.
tags.look: Campaigns that won (or lost) concessions, insider vs outsider groups, strikes, protests, lobbying rows.

tags.name: Rights in context
tags.about: How rights are protected or restricted in the UK: the Human Rights Act, ECHR, Equality Act, protest law, free speech.
tags.look: Protest restrictions, proscription, ECHR rows, judicial reviews on rights, free-speech disputes, the EHRC.

tags.name: Labour, Conservatives & Lib Dems
tags.about: The established parties: their ideas, policies, factions, leaders and conferences.
tags.look: Party conferences, factional fights (e.g. Labour left vs right), policy shifts, leadership positioning.

tags.name: Emerging & minor parties
tags.about: Reform UK, the Greens, SNP, Plaid Cymru, NI parties, Your Party, Restore Britain and other challengers.
tags.look: Poll surges, by-election and council wins, defections, minor parties in devolved government.

tags.name: Party system, funding & leadership
tags.about: How parties are funded and organised, leadership contests, defections, and whether the UK is now multi-party.
tags.look: Big donations, funding rules, membership figures, leadership elections, defections, polls showing fragmentation.

tags.name: Electoral systems & elections
tags.about: FPTP, AMS, STV, SV and closed list systems, how they perform, and UK elections as evidence.
tags.look: Disproportional results, by-elections, devolved/mayoral election outcomes, electoral reform campaigns.

tags.name: Referendums
tags.about: How referendums are used in the UK and the arguments for and against them.
tags.look: Calls for independence referendums, border poll debates, local referendums, Brexit referendum legacy.

tags.name: Voting behaviour & polls
tags.about: Why people vote as they do: class, age, education, region, leaders, issues; polls and election case studies.
tags.look: Poll leads and demographic splits, leader ratings, analysis of why a party won or lost.

tags.name: Media influence
tags.about: The role of TV, the press and social media in shaping opinion, elections and political agendas.
tags.look: Ofcom rulings, BBC governance and impartiality rows, social media & misinformation, press investigations.

tags.name: Constitution: sources & reform
tags.about: The uncodified constitution, conventions, the prerogative, and reforms such as Lords reform.
tags.look: Constitutional reforms, conventions being tested or broken, codification debates, monarchy and prerogative.

3: reform of the House of Lords

tags.name: Devolution
tags.about: The Scottish Parliament, Senedd, NI Assembly and English devolution (mayors, strategic authorities) and their impact.
tags.look: Devolved governments' decisions, rows with Westminster, independence debates, English mayors' powers.

tags.name: Commons & scrutiny
tags.about: MPs, the Commons and how Parliament scrutinises government: PMQs, select committees, rebellions, the whips.
tags.look: Rebellions, select committee hearings and reports, urgent questions, humble addresses, the Speaker.

tags.name: House of Lords
tags.about: The Lords' composition, powers and legitimacy; defeats and amendments; reform.
tags.look: Lords defeats, ping-pong, appointments rows, hereditary peers, Salisbury convention, Parliament Acts.

tags.name: Legislative process
tags.about: How bills become law: readings, committee and report stages, Lords amendments, royal assent, private members' bills.
tags.look: Bills moving through stages, amendments, free votes, private members' bills, secondary legislation.

tags.name: PM, cabinet & executive power
tags.about: The Prime Minister's power, the cabinet, No 10, the civil service and how the executive makes policy.
tags.look: Reshuffles, No 10 power struggles, U-turns, special advisers, the Budget, PM–cabinet relations.

tags.name: Ministerial responsibility
tags.about: Individual and collective ministerial responsibility: resignations, sackings, the ministerial code, cabinet splits.
tags.look: Ministers resigning or refusing to, code breaches, ethics adviser rulings, collective responsibility suspended.

tags.name: Supreme Court & judiciary
tags.about: The UK Supreme Court and senior judges: judicial review, independence, neutrality and influence on policy.
tags.look: Judicial reviews against ministers, Supreme Court judgments with political impact, clashes over the rule of law.

tags.name: Executive–Parliament balance
tags.about: Who has the upper hand, government or Parliament? Majorities, defeats, concessions, 'elective dictatorship'.
tags.look: Government defeats or forced U-turns, big majorities pushing bills through, confidence votes.

tags.name: The EU & the UK
tags.about: The EU's aims and its impact on UK government before and after Brexit, including the UK–EU 'reset'.
tags.look: Reset deals (SPS/agrifood, youth scheme, Erasmus+), alignment with EU rules, Windsor Framework, rejoin debates.

tags.name: Location of sovereignty
tags.about: Where sovereignty lies: Parliament, the people, the executive, devolved bodies, the EU (past) and the ECHR.
tags.look: ECHR exit pledges, Brexit sovereignty claims, referendums as popular sovereignty, devolution tensions.

tags.name: Conservatism
tags.about: Tradition, pragmatism, human imperfection, organic society, paternalism; one-nation vs New Right.
tags.look: One-nation vs New Right tensions, tax cuts and small-state arguments, law-and-order and tradition debates.

tags.name: Liberalism
tags.about: Individualism, liberty, limited government, rationalism, social justice; classical vs modern liberalism.
tags.look: Free speech and civil liberty debates, welfare-state arguments, equality of opportunity, liberal democracy under strain.

tags.name: Socialism
tags.about: Collectivism, common humanity, equality, social class, workers' control; revolutionary socialism, social democracy, Third Way.
tags.look: Nationalisation and public ownership, wealth taxes, workers' rights, inequality, debates on Labour's direction.

tags.name: Anarchism
tags.about: Rejection of the state, liberty, 'anarchy is order', economic freedom; collectivist vs individualist anarchism.
tags.look: Anti-state movements, mutual aid, direct-action groups that reject state authority.

tags.name: Ecologism
tags.about: Ecology, holism, environmental ethics, sustainability; deep vs shallow green, social ecology.
tags.look: Net zero politics, degrowth vs green growth, climate activism, biodiversity policy.

tags.name: Feminism
tags.about: Sex and gender, patriarchy, 'the personal is political', equality vs difference feminism, intersectionality.
tags.look: Gender pay gap, violence against women, representation of women, debates over sex and gender.

tags.name: Multiculturalism
tags.about: Politics of recognition, culture and identity, minority rights, diversity; liberal, pluralist and cosmopolitan multiculturalism.
tags.look: Integration and cohesion debates, minority rights, responses to racism and religious hatred.

tags.name: Nationalism
tags.about: Nations, self-determination, the nation-state, culturalism; liberal, conservative, anti-colonial and expansionist nationalism.
tags.look: Independence movements, patriotism and flag politics, far-right nationalism, expansionist claims on territory.

tags.name: The Constitution
tags.about: The nature and principles of the US Constitution: separation of powers, checks and balances, amendments, interpretation.
tags.look: Constitutional clashes between branches, amendment-based disputes, originalism vs living constitution.

tags.name: Federalism
tags.about: The balance of power between Washington and the states — and fights over it.
tags.look: National Guard deployments, sanctuary cities, states suing the federal government, state laws diverging.

tags.name: Congress
tags.about: The House and Senate: structure, legislation, representation, oversight, the power of the purse.
tags.look: Shutdowns and spending fights, filibuster, discharge petitions, hearings and subpoenas, war powers votes.

tags.name: Presidency
tags.about: Formal and informal powers of the president, relations with other branches, limits on presidential power.
tags.look: Executive orders, emergency powers, tariffs, pardons, firing officials, military action without Congress, approval ratings.

tags.name: Supreme Court
tags.about: The Supreme Court's role, appointments and impact on public policy; judicial activism vs restraint.
tags.look: Major rulings and their vote splits, emergency-docket orders, nominations, originalism vs living constitution.

tags.name: Civil rights & liberties
tags.about: Protection of civil liberties and rights today, including race and rights, voting rights, immigration and LGBTQ+ rights.
tags.look: Voting Rights Act cases, affirmative action/DEI, immigration enforcement, abortion, guns, free speech, trans rights.

tags.name: Elections & campaign finance
tags.about: Presidential and congressional elections, primaries, redistricting, incumbency and campaign finance.
tags.look: Midterm races, primary upsets, gerrymandering fights, super PAC spending, voting-rule changes.

tags.name: Parties
tags.about: Ideas and principles of Democrats and Republicans, factions and conflicts within them, coalitions of supporters.
tags.look: MAGA vs establishment, progressive vs moderate Democrats, party leadership rows, polarisation.

tags.name: Interest groups
tags.about: Interest groups' methods and influence: lobbying, litigation, campaign spending, grassroots mobilisation.
tags.look: Lobby spending, groups backing lawsuits, PAC money in primaries, big industry lobbies (crypto, AI, guns).

tags.name: UK–US comparisons
tags.about: Stories that link the UK and US systems — useful for comparative (rational, cultural, structural) answers.
tags.look: UK–US relations, similar debates in both countries (e.g. courts vs executives, populism, party splits).

tags.name: State, sovereignty & globalisation
tags.about: The nation-state and sovereignty; economic, political and cultural globalisation and its impact on states.
tags.look: Tariffs and trade wars, supply-chain shocks, migration, cyber and AI governance, territorial disputes.

tags.name: UN & NATO
tags.about: The UN (Security Council, General Assembly, Secretary-General, peacekeeping) and NATO: roles and effectiveness.
tags.look: Security Council vetoes and resolutions, UN reform and funding, the Secretary-General race, NATO summits and Article 4/5.

tags.name: IMF, World Bank, WTO, G7/G20
tags.about: Global economic governance: the IMF, World Bank, WTO, G7 and G20, trade, debt and global poverty.
tags.look: Trade disputes and deals, IMF loans, debt crises, aid cuts, G7/G20 summits, BRICS finance.

tags.name: Human rights & international law
tags.about: The ICJ, ICC and human rights regime; humanitarian intervention and the responsibility to protect.
tags.look: ICC/ICJ cases and warrants, war crimes allegations, humanitarian crises, interventions and their legitimacy.

tags.name: Environmental governance
tags.about: Global climate governance: the UNFCCC, COP summits, the Paris Agreement, and why cooperation is hard.
tags.look: COP negotiations, national pledges (NDCs), climate finance, withdrawals from agreements, record temperatures.

tags.name: Power & polarity
tags.about: Types of power, great and emerging powers, polarity (uni/bi/multipolar), state systems and global developments.
tags.look: US–China rivalry, Russia's war, rising powers and BRICS, uses of hard/soft power, authoritarian vs democratic states.

tags.name: Regionalism & the EU
tags.about: Regional organisations (EU, ASEAN, AU, Arab League, USMCA) — integration, enlargement and global influence.
tags.look: EU sanctions and trade deals, enlargement, EU defence moves, divisions between member states, ASEAN/AU action.

tags.name: Realism vs liberalism
tags.about: How realist and liberal theories explain events: state self-interest and power vs cooperation, institutions and interdependence.
tags.look: 'Rules-based order' debates, unilateral vs multilateral action, cooperation through institutions, security dilemmas.
